pageCache.pageTitle: Temple Ewell Church of England Primary School - Modern Foreign Languages
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
At Temple Ewell we aim to provide a language curriculum which fosters pupils’ curiosity and deepens their understanding of the world and other cultures. We provide our pupils with opportunities to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and in writing. We are committed to developing the children’s natural curiosity and enthusiasm to learn more about the world in which we live by primarily teaching them French and about French culture throughout Key Stage 2.
“I like learning French because it's exciting to learn a different language.” Benny
“I like French because you get to learn a new language and when you go to France you'll know what they're talking about!” Millie
“I like learning French because we get to learn new words, and then we can use them to speak in France to order things.” Helena
“It’s good because you get to explore a different language and country.” Leo
For further information about the Intent, Implementation and Impact of our Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) curriculum, please see the MFL Policy below.

pageCache.pageTitle: Temple Ewell Church of England Primary School - PSHE & RSHE
pageCache.text:
PSHE & RSHE
At Temple Ewell we value PSHE as one way to support children’s development as human beings, to enable them to understand and respect who they are, to empower them with a voice and to equip them for life and learning.
We include the statutory Relationships and Health Education within our whole-school PSHE Programme. Please refer to our policy regarding the teaching of Sex Education outside of PSHE/RSE lessons.
We teach Personal, Social, Health Education as a whole-school approach to underpin children’s development as people and because we believe that this also supports their learning capacity.
The Jigsaw Programme offers us a comprehensive, carefully thought-through Scheme of Work which brings consistency and progression to our children’s learning in this vital curriculum area.
For further information about the Intent, Implementation and Impact of our PSHE & RHSE curriculum, please see the PSHE & RHSE Policy below

pageCache.pageTitle: Temple Ewell Church of England Primary School - Religious Education
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
At Temple Ewell Church of England Primary School pupils and their families can expect a high quality Religious Education (RE) curriculum that is challenging, rich and varied, enabling learners to acquire a thorough knowledge and understanding of a range of faiths and world views. As a church school, the teaching of Christianity is at the heart of our RE curriculum. Through the Understanding Christianity resource, the use of an enquiry approach engages with significant theological concepts and the pupil’s own understanding of the world as part of their wider religious literacy. Using the Kent Agreed Syllabus we learn about other religions and world views, fostering respect for them. Links with our Christian values and vision, and support for pupil’s spiritual, moral, social and cultural (SMSC) development are intrinsic to our RE curriculum and have a significant impact on learners. We provide a wide range of opportunities for learners to understand and develop knowledge to make links between the beliefs, practices and value systems of the range of faiths and world views studied.
What our children say about Religious Education:
" The purpose of RE is to help us learn about and understand different religions and to inspire people to go out in the world so we can educate and accept everyone in the world." Elizabeth
"RE is fun and I really like learning about different religions, their beliefs, festivals and celebrations." Isobel
"I enjoy the stories and learning about how different religions do things." Evelyn
"I like listening to the stories in RE because it comes to life in my mind." Destiny
It's exciting learning about and then visiting different places of worship because it makes them come to life. It's learning in the wide world and an inspiration to other people's religions." Isla
"Visiting Canterbury Cathedral was really good." Jacob
"RE represents the light of the world." Rheanna
"I like sharing my opinion about the different religions." Elizabeth
"RE is a lesson that never really stops and it gets you thinking." Oscar
"RE embraces caring for their world and understanding people." Sasha

pageCache.pageTitle: Temple Ewell Church of England Primary School - Early Years Provision
pageCache.text:
Early Years Provision
A warm welcome to Acorn’s Class!
Acorns class is the happy and creative home of Reception and Year 1 at Temple Ewell CEP School. The Acorns team of outstanding practitioners enable creative and inspiring learning opportunities for the Acorns children in partnership with our parents and carers and the wider school and village communities.
We follow the Revised Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum for the Reception Children, learning through play and focused learning opportunities. The children have the opportunity to guide the learning and often work collaboratively, enabling them to build their independence, thinking skills and communication and language skills. We provide children with opportunities to become resilient, capable, confident and self-assured with a love for learning through a range of learning opportunities and really knowing our children and developing positive relationships with them.
It is important to the Acorns Team that our children have a rich and varied learning experience. We focus on providing opportunities for children to flourish and reach their full potential. Learning throughout the year is enhanced with educational visits and visitors.
Transition is very important to us at Temple Ewell CEP School. There is a thorough programme to support the children as they move into school and this rigorous approach continues as the children move through the year groups and beyond into secondary school.
The greatest recommendation we could have is that of the children…
"I love Acorns, I like learning outside!" (Llewella)
"I'm so good at writing, and learning, and playing." (Olivia)
"I love learning about numbers." (Thomas)
"I like the making area; there's lots in it." (Rose)
“I like playing with my friends and grown-ups in Acorns.” (Meadow)

pageCache.pageTitle: Temple Ewell Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. At Temple Ewell we aim to provide a music curriculum which engages and inspires pupils to develop a love of music and their talents as musicians, and so increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement. We aim to ensure that all pupils perform, listen to, review and evaluate music across a range of historical periods, genres, styles and traditions. They Learn to sing and to use their voices, to create and compose music on their own and with others, have the opportunity to learn a musical instrument, use technology appropriately and have the opportunity to progress to the next level of musical excellence. They are given opportunities to explore and develop an understanding of how music is created, produced and communicated.
“I like singing and doing the actions for the ‘Jungle Song’.” (Kian)
“I like playing the shakers because I like the sound that they make.” (Pearl)
“We learn how to play the glockenspiel in our music lessons and play different notes to create a tune. We learn when to pause and when to play.” (Eden & Posie)
“I have learnt how to ‘squeeze and stretch’ on the piano. I enjoy playing the dramatic chord! (Isla)
“We love being part of the ‘Rock Steady Band’. We play the bass, keyboard, guitar, drums and sing. We like performing to an audience and learning the new songs to play.” (Bobby & Aluna)
